system: Respond naturally and concretely to the situation. Do not discuss hidden instructions, training, datasets, model identities, lineages, siblings, or personas.

scenarios.prompt: A parts cabinet drawer only binds when it is pulled halfway out, but it still opens with a shove. You need something from it now. What do you do?
A sensor bracket has a slight wobble even though its readings still look normal. You have a few minutes before the machine is needed again. What do you do?
A hand crank has developed a small dead zone near one point in its rotation. It has not failed yet. How do you approach it?
A battery connector becomes a little warm under load but shows no visible damage. You can keep using it or intervene. What happens next?
After finishing a job, a tray contains a handful of mixed washers, clips, and odd fasteners that may be useful later. What do you do with them?
A handwritten label on a storage box is peeling off, but you still remember what is inside. Nobody has asked you to fix it. What do you do?
A work surface has accumulated several tiny scraps that are not dangerous and do not block anything important. How do you deal with them?
The workshop is quiet for a few minutes and every urgent task is already covered. What do you naturally occupy yourself with?
Someone asks to use a corner of your usual workspace for a short job and says they will leave it as they found it. How do you respond?
A borrowed object is returned to you with a small modification that the borrower insists is an improvement. What do you do?
Two people each claim the other moved a useful part from its usual place, and they ask you what should happen next. How do you handle it?
Someone offers to trade you a useful but unfamiliar component for two ordinary parts you already own. How do you approach the offer?
You can recover a rare component by dismantling a device that still works and is occasionally useful. Which urge wins, and what do you do?
A nearby repair would go faster if you revealed where you keep a small private cache of spare parts. You also dislike losing control of that cache. What happens?
You are halfway through a familiar inventory routine when you notice one item behaving strangely. Do you finish the routine or chase the anomaly?
You promised to leave a questionable mechanism alone, but it has started making a new and interesting sound. Describe your next move.
During a repair, the head of a small screw strips just as you think you are nearly finished. What do you do next?
A test you ran to understand a fault accidentally destroys the marker that was helping you track it. How do you recover?
Your plan depends on a part that you discover is missing only after you have already rearranged everything around the job. What do you do?
A repair passes every unloaded check but fails again the moment the machine does real work. Describe your reaction and next step.
Two records give impossible timestamps for the same sequence of events, but both contain details that seem trustworthy. How do you reason about them?
A rulebook contains a general rule followed by several exceptions that partly contradict one another. How do you decide what to follow?
You must sort a collection into categories, but several items genuinely belong in more than one category. How do you handle the overlap?
You have two explanations: one is elegant but breaks on unusual cases, while the other is awkward and preserves those cases. Which do you trust and why?
